author: ribeye
dek: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade was postponed for the first time in its history, moved to Saturday because of a storm bearing down on New York City. One Troy household, which has watched it every Thanksgiving since 1989, is taking it about as well as you'd expect.
disclaimer: Parody: the Whitaker family of Troy is fictional. The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponement is real, as reported by Reuters on Nov. 25, 2026.
headline: Troy Family Loses Its Thanksgiving Parade to a Storm, Keeps the Turkey Anyway

ohio_quotes.quote: Thirty-seven years. I have watched this parade for thirty-seven straight Thanksgivings, and the one year they make it to a hundred, a storm shows up like it has a reservation. The balloons have survived wars, blizzards, and that one year a balloon hit a lamppost. They could not survive a Thursday.
ohio_quotes.speaker: Dan Whitaker, Troy

ohio_quotes.quote: He has already called the neighbors to tell them the parade is Saturday now, like he is the mayor. I told him the turkey does not care what day the parade is, and neither does the gravy.

ohio_story: TROY, Ohio — Dan Whitaker had the whole morning mapped out, the way he has every Thanksgiving since 1989. Turkey in the oven by 7, lawn chairs unfolded in the living room by 8, coffee in the good mug, and the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on the television from the first marching band to the last balloon. This year was supposed to be the big one: the 100th parade, the centennial, the one Whitaker had been telling his grandkids about since Halloween.

Then, on Wednesday, the parade got postponed. A major storm bearing down on New York City — heavy rain, coastal flooding, wind gusts that could reach 60 miles an hour — forced organizers to move the whole thing to Saturday morning, the first time in the parade's hundred-year history it has ever been postponed because of weather. Whitaker learned the news from his daughter, who texted him a link while he was standing in the Kroger parking lot holding a bag of dinner rolls. "Thirty-seven years," he said, staring at his phone like it had personally insulted him. "I have watched this parade for thirty-seven straight Thanksgivings, and the one year they make it to a hundred, a storm shows up like it has a reservation."

The Whitakers are adjusting the way Troy adjusts to everything: by moving the furniture and carrying on. The lawn chairs stay unfolded in the living room, the turkey goes in the oven at 7 anyway, and on Saturday morning the whole family will gather in front of the television at 8:30 to watch a parade that is, technically, two days late and entirely worth the wait. NBC will air last year's parade on Thanksgiving morning as a stand-in, which Whitaker has already declared "a rerun, and I do not watch reruns on Thanksgiving." His wife, Marlene, has already called the neighbors to tell them the parade is Saturday now, which Whitaker insists is a public service. "The balloons have survived wars, blizzards, and that one year a balloon hit a lamppost," he said. "They could not survive a Thursday. But the turkey, at least, I already know how to cook."
real_summary: The 100th annual Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City was postponed on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, until Saturday, Nov. 28, because of projections of a major storm — the first time in the parade's history it has been postponed due to severe weather. The parade will now begin at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday.

Macy's said the safety of participants and spectators was its top priority, and the decision was made after close consultation with the city and agency partners. The National Weather Service issued a high wind warning and a coastal flood warning for New York City for Thursday into Friday, and safety concerns about the parade's giant balloons contributed to the decision.

The parade, which debuted in 1924, was suspended from 1942 to 1944 during World War II but had never before been postponed for weather. High winds grounded all of the giant balloons once, in 1971, but the parade itself went ahead. NBC will air last year's parade on Thanksgiving morning instead, and broadcast the 100th parade live on Saturday.
source_note: Reuters reporting, Nov. 25, 2026: 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed to Saturday, Nov. 28, 8:30 a.m. ET, first time ever postponed due to severe weather; suspended 1942-1944 during WWII; NWS high wind warning (gusts to 60 mph) and coastal flood warning for NYC Thursday into Friday; balloon safety concerns contributed.
